comment: The recorded-invocation gate. Each scenario is one offline invocation: argv, environment, and recorded responses. The stage 1 scenarios were generated by the TypeScript implementation this package replaced and remain the cross-language parity gate (docs/design/v1-python.md §5); the stage 2 host, vuln, and scopes scenarios and the stage 3 NG-SIEM search scenarios are regression pins generated from this implementation. Four stage 1 documents changed at stage 2 (help-top, unknown-command, home-view, home-view-no-credential) because the command surface grew to the one docs/design/v1.md §1.4 specifies, and eight changed at stage 3 (those four plus scopes, auth-status, auth-status-member-cid, auth-status-retargeted) because captain exception N1 added the NG-SIEM search surface and the NGSIEM:write scope it requires (docs/design/v1.md §4.3). help-vuln-list changed when vuln list gained --fields (docs/design/v1.md §10). help-top, unknown-command, home-view, and scopes changed when cve show shipped: the command list, the home suggestion, and the license-gated Falcon Intelligence scope (docs/design/v1.md §2.2). Stage 4 slice B added the identity scenarios and changed help-top, unknown-command, scopes, and the three auth-status documents that print a scope line, because captain exception N2 added the `identity` noun and the Identity Protection GraphQL:write scope it requires (docs/design/v1.md §4.4). host-list-filtered and identity-list changed to shell-safe continuation quoting, preserving wildcard arguments literally (docs/design/v1.md §7.2). identity-list's cursor changed to bind an unambiguous JSON filter tuple (docs/design/v1.md §4.4), and scopes changed to describe only the effect of omitting NGSIEM:write, without claiming the remaining GraphQL write permission is read-only (docs/design/v1.md §5.7). help-search-start and help-search-stop changed to state their NGSIEM:write requirement without claiming it is the tool's only write scope (docs/design/v1.md §4.3). The base Falcon Identity slice added host logins and account scenarios (design section 2.2), changing help-top, unknown-command, unknown-host-subcommand, and scopes to describe that surface. Its fixes narrowed host logins to one device id and carried global context into actionable error remedies. Identity slice A adds identity-activity, identity detection, and --product scenarios (docs/design/v1.md sections 4.3 and 10.2). Its help, command-discovery, home, auth, and scopes changes are combined with slice B rather than replacing that surface. help-identity-activity states only its command-specific NGSIEM:write requirement, without claiming it is the tool's only write scope (section 4.3). Identity detection rows include account_id and device_id and omit the unrequested source_ip field. Shared suggestions preserve literal FQL and backticks, explicit region and origin opt-in, and tenant selection without printing a standalone CID (section 7.2). The AXI credential migration deliberately changes help-top, unknown-command, unknown-flag, unknown-flag-global, and list-with-positional to advertise the shipped profile list/config path commands and their global flags; profile-refused becomes profile-not-found because profile selection now ships. home-view-no-credential and auth-status-no-credential now report PROFILE_REQUIRED and the config.json/SecretRef setup; the latter exits 1. auth-status, auth-status-member-cid, and auth-status-retargeted now include profile, endpoint, and secret source. These contract changes are specified in docs/design/v1.md sections 5.2 and 12.1; the remaining recorded documents are unchanged.
stable_encoder_comment: Adopting toon-format>=1.2,<2 deliberately changes only hash-prefixed CQL quoting in search-start, search-status-done, and search-status-empty (docs/design/v1.md section 10.1 and v1-python.md section 8).
version_comment: The three version scenarios pin bare-version output for -v, -V, and --version. Only their release number is substituted at comparison time, like the help-top banner. help-top, home-view, home-view-no-credential, and home-view-skill-hint now name every shipped read domain, including indicators (docs/design/v1.md section 12.1).
indicator_comment: Intel indicator list/show adds marker continuation scenarios and changes help-top, unknown-command, and scopes to advertise the shipped read-only surface (design sections 7.1 and 7.2).
pagination_comment: The shipped bounded walker (docs/design/v1.md sections 7.2 and 10.2) adds three wholly synthetic partial-read examples. The four list help documents, unknown-flag, and list-with-positional deliberately change to advertise --all and --max-rows. Existing data documents and scopes remain unchanged because no operation or permission changed.
fields_comment: Detection and host field selection adds extended-row scenarios and updates help-detection-list, help-host-list, unknown-flag, and list-with-positional to advertise the shipped flag (design section 10.2).
detection_summary_comment: Detection summary adds on-demand severity scenarios and updates help-top, unknown-command, unknown-detection-subcommand, and scopes (design section 10.3); the home view makes no aggregate request.
intel_comment: Actor and report read commands add Intel scenarios and deliberately change help-top, unknown-command, scopes, and auth status scope lines to include Actors and Reports (Falcon Intelligence):read, as specified in docs/design/v1.md section 2.3. MITRE is JSON only; no downloads or writes are admitted.
batch_1_comment: The combined CVE/Spotlight, identity assessment/sensor, Discover inventory, custom IOC/host-group, and policy read surfaces deliberately extend help-top, unknown-command, and scopes together. Their contracts are in docs/design/v1.md sections 1.2, 1.4.1, 1.7, 2.2, and 4.4. The shared documents were replayed once after integration; existing per-command documents retain their byte comparisons.
